# Disagreement Log — Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 14

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 29

---

## Disagreements

**v. 1** — "savage waves" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "violence of the sea" (PNEUMA). EMET/LOGOS follow the Greek ἄγρια κύματα more literally. SOPHIA: "savage waves."

**v. 2** — "a longing for gain" (EMET) vs. "desire for gain" (LOGOS) vs. "human greed" (PNEUMA). PNEUMA's expansion is interpretive; LOGOS's rendering adopted.

**v. 3** — "pilots it" (EMET) vs. "steers it" (LOGOS, PNEUMA). Minor; LOGOS/PNEUMA preferred.

**v. 5** — "works of your wisdom should not be idle" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "wisdom's works to lie idle" (PNEUMA). EMET/LOGOS closer to Greek; adopted.

**v. 6** — "arrogant giants" — all three agree on this translation of ὑπερήφανοι γίγαντες. No dispute on the Noah reference.

**v. 8** — EMET: "handmade idol is accursed, both it and the one who made it — he because he made it, and it because it was called a god." LOGOS: cleaner dash structure. PNEUMA: "carved by human hands is cursed." SOPHIA adopts LOGOS structure with EMET's "handmade."

**v. 9** — "equally hateful to God" — all three agree on basic sense; no structural dispute.

**v. 11** — EMET: "idols of the nations." LOGOS: "idols of the nations." PNEUMA: "idols of the nations." Agreement on noun; PNEUMA adds "even the idols" for emphasis, rejected as addition.

**v. 12** — "spiritual fornication" (EMET) vs. "fornication" (LOGOS) vs. "spiritual adultery" (PNEUMA). The Greek πορνείας does not include "spiritual" — it is supplied. EMET and PNEUMA both add the qualifier. SOPHIA: "spiritual fornication" follows longstanding interpretive tradition.

**v. 14** — "empty boasting" (EMET) vs. "empty vanity" (LOGOS) vs. "empty arrogance" (PNEUMA). Greek κενοδοξίᾳ = vainglory/empty conceit. LOGOS's "vanity" adopted.

**v. 15** — EMET: "afflicted with grief at an untimely bereavement." LOGOS: "consumed with grief over a child taken untimely." PNEUMA: "shattered by grief over a child snatched away too soon." This key verse: PNEUMA's rendering most vivid; LOGOS structure cleaner. SOPHIA adopts LOGOS with "consumed."

**v. 15** — "mysteries and initiations" (EMET) vs. "secret rites and ceremonies" (LOGOS) vs. "secret rites and solemn ceremonies" (PNEUMA). EMET preserves "initiations" (τελετάς). SOPHIA: "secret rites and initiations."

**v. 16** — "ungodly custom became strong" (EMET) vs. "ungodly custom was strengthened" (LOGOS) vs. "godless custom hardened into law" (PNEUMA). LOGOS adopted.

**v. 17** — "imagined the distant appearance" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "imagined his face" (PNEUMA). PNEUMA simplifies; EMET/LOGOS closer to Greek εἰκόνα τοῦ τιμωμένου βασιλέως. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.

**v. 18** — "ambition of the craftsman advanced even those who did not know him in worship" (EMET) vs. "ambition of the craftsman drove the cult further" (PNEUMA). PNEUMA expands. LOGOS: "ambition of the craftsman drove even those who did not know the king." SOPHIA: LOGOS version.

**v. 19** — "force the likeness to look finer" (EMET) vs. "pressed his art to produce a finer likeness" (LOGOS) vs. "force his skill to produce a likeness more beautiful" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 20** — "now considered as an object of worship" (EMET) vs. "came to regard as an object of devotion" (LOGOS) vs. "came to worship" (PNEUMA). "worship" too blunt at this stage; LOGOS's "object of devotion" or EMET's "object of worship" both work. SOPHIA: "object of worship."

**v. 21** — "the incommunicable Name" (EMET) vs. "the Name that cannot be shared" (LOGOS) vs. "the Name that belongs to no one else" (PNEUMA). The Greek ἀκοινώνητον ὄνομα means "not held in common / not shareable." LOGOS: most literal. SOPHIA: "the Name that cannot be shared."

**v. 21** — "enslaved either to calamity or to tyranny" (EMET) vs. "enslaved either to misfortune or to tyranny" (LOGOS) vs. "in the grip of grief, or crushed under tyranny" (PNEUMA). PNEUMA diverges significantly. LOGOS: "misfortune" for πάθει. SOPHIA: LOGOS.

**v. 22** — "great conflict of ignorance" (EMET) vs. "great war of ignorance" (LOGOS, PNEUMA). "war" for πόλεμον preferred.

**v. 23** — "holding frenzied revels of strange ordinances" (EMET) vs. "frenzied revels with outlandish ceremonies" (LOGOS) vs. "wild midnight revels" (PNEUMA). PNEUMA adds "midnight" — not in text. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 24** — "purity of life or the sanctity of marriage" (LOGOS) vs. "lives or marriages pure" (EMET) vs. "purity of life and purity of marriage" (PNEUMA). LOGOS adopted.

**v. 25–26** — Vice list: minor variation in order and wording. All three largely agree. PNEUMA adds interpretive commentary ("souls rotted through") — adjusted to "pollution of souls."

**v. 27** — "idols that may not be named" (EMET) vs. "unspeakable idols" (LOGOS) vs. "nameless idols" (PNEUMA). Greek ἀνωνύμων = without name / unnameable. SOPHIA: "idols whose names may not be uttered."

**v. 28** — "celebrate in exaltation" (EMET) vs. "make merry in exultation" (LOGOS) vs. "work themselves into a frenzy of ecstasy" (PNEUMA). PNEUMA expansive. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 29** — "trust in lifeless idols" — all three agree; no dispute.

**v. 30** — "thought wrongly about God" (EMET, SOPHIA) vs. "thought perversely about God" (LOGOS) vs. "were wrong about God" (PNEUMA). EMET's "wrongly" or LOGOS's "perversely" for εφρόνησαν. SOPHIA: "thought wrongly."

**v. 31** — "just penalty for those who sin" (EMET) vs. "just penalty of sinners" (LOGOS) vs. "just punishment that always dogs the footsteps" (PNEUMA). PNEUMA's idiom ("dogs the footsteps") vivid but too informal. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 31** — "transgression of the unrighteous" — all three agree; no dispute.
